captions.linkedin:
A coding agent managed by a harness can replace MCP, and the reason is straightforward: token cost.

With MCP always connected, tokens are spent whether the tool is needed or not. A harness changes that. It defines which tools the agent may use, when, and how. The agent calls a tool only when it decides it needs one, via a terminal command, and a human approves before anything runs.

A real example: Claude Code working with GitHub through commands, with no MCP in the loop.

There is a line where MCP still makes sense. Knowing that line is the practical skill.

More on agent architecture at metaxis.io
